# Simone Weil quote sources

8 passages attributed to Simone Weil in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Weil.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Simone Weil

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

French

Cited here from

Gravity and Grace, Waiting for God, the letter to Joë Bousquet of 13 April 1942, and The Iliad, or the Poem of Force.

How to cite it

Check whether the piece is something Weil finished and published. The Iliad essay (1940–41, published under the pseudonym Émile Novis) is; most of the rest of the corpus is posthumous and was arranged by editors, so the book title is not a source in the ordinary sense.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Gravity and Grace was assembled after her death by Gustave Thibon from her notebooks, and its chapter structure is his. A sentence can therefore appear in Gravity and Grace without appearing in anything Weil published or completed, and the book's arrangement suggests a systematic treatise she never wrote. Naming the editor's organisation as the source is more accurate than naming her.

1 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Simone Weil?

Check whether the piece is something Weil finished and published. The Iliad essay (1940–41, published under the pseudonym Émile Novis) is; most of the rest of the corpus is posthumous and was arranged by editors, so the book title is not a source in the ordinary sense. This archive cites Simone Weil from Gravity and Grace, Waiting for God, the letter to Joë Bousquet of 13 April 1942, and The Iliad, or the Poem of Force. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Simone Weil?

Gravity and Grace was assembled after her death by Gustave Thibon from her notebooks, and its chapter structure is his. A sentence can therefore appear in Gravity and Grace without appearing in anything Weil published or completed, and the book's arrangement suggests a systematic treatise she never wrote. Naming the editor's organisation as the source is more accurate than naming her.

### What language did Simone Weil write in?

French. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
